candidates.tagline: Trinity axed their famous tower logo. Replacement looks like Days Inn.
candidates.story: Trinity University (San Antonio) unveiled a new 'sunburst' logo on July 30, 2026, retiring the Murchison Tower it had used since 2003; alumni immediately compared the generic starburst to logos for Days Inn, La Quinta, and Frost Bank — and the university paused its rollout on August 4 after the backlash overwhelmed social media, postponing a planned brand-launch celebration.
candidates.why_funny: A university spent money hiring designers to replace a distinctive landmark with something indistinguishable from a mid-tier hotel chain, then got so embarrassed it pulled the logo before the official launch party.
candidates.alt: Trinity University's Murchison Tower — the slender red-brick bell tower standing tall above surrounding trees, reflected in a campus pool — the iconic campus landmark erased from the new logo

candidates.tagline: Ford's 'Model T moment': a truck so new you can't see it until 2027.
candidates.story: Ford CEO Jim Farley announced on August 6, 2026 that the 'Fathom,' a $28,350 electric pickup truck, represents Ford's 'Model T moment' and 'breakthrough electric vehicle' — but the actual truck design won't be revealed until early 2027, so the announcement image is literally just the name badge on a black surface while critics said the compact pickup doesn't address the right market.
candidates.why_funny: Ford declared a historic 'Model T moment' for a truck they are not yet allowed to show anyone, which means their generation-defining breakthrough currently looks like a hotel room safe.
candidates.alt: The Ford 'FATHOM' name badge — white letters spelling FATHOM™ on a black rectangular metal plate against a dark textured background — the entire visual announcement for Ford's declared 'Model T moment'
